notes: Car 4a — software-face parity closes the remaining capability-surface gaps from the feature survey, plus the ten small adoption items folded in from the research table. (1) OpenAI-compatible API server on the loopback console: GET /v1/models and POST /v1/chat/completions (streaming and non-streaming) behind a dedicated OPENAI_API_TOKEN secrets slot (missing slot = 503 naming the slot, wrong key = 401, OpenAI-shaped error bodies), running the same agent loop as the console chat — system stack, tools, failover — as a stateless gateway: client messages are folded into one turn (last user message as input, earlier turns as history, tool/function roles dropped), client-supplied tools are accepted but not executed, the requested model field is echoed back as the actually configured model, and usage is reported as a documented chars/4 approximation because no tokenizer exists (never claimed exact). (2) GET /api/capabilities: a read-only catalog of tools, skills, channel state, hook events and cron count, with an automated assertion that no secrets.env slot value appears in the response. (3) Event hooks: a validated settings block drives six whitelisted events (turn_start/turn_end/tool_call/compact/cron_fire/error); hooks are argv arrays executed without a shell on background threads with 1-30s timeouts, a minimal environment whitelist, chat ids redacted before reaching the hook, output that never echoes into chat, and full isolation — a failing or timed-out hook can never block or alter a turn. (4) ACP server (python3 -m mycore.acp): stdio JSON-RPC protocol version 1 with initialize, session/new, streamed session/prompt updates and cancel, plus the agent-to-client fs read/write proxy (the client owns the files); terminal capability is deliberately not declared and no session persistence is claimed. (5) modeltier v2: credential pools (comma-separated key slots per upstream, rotate to the next untried slot on 401/403 with exactly-once-per-slot discipline), per-key health with exponential in-process cooldown (all-cold still tries the least-cold candidate — never a silent dead end), cached-token passthrough when the upstream returns one, and a deterministic system-prefix test; in-memory only, no queue timeouts and no cache_control injection, both stated as out of scope. (6) Research-table folds: relative countdowns in /cron lists (language-neutral), per-task model selection for the delegate tool validated against the configured model list with an honest per-task error block (never a silent fallback), forum-topic session isolation for Telegram (per-topic session keys, replies carry the thread id; cross-topic context transfer is explicitly v1 out of scope), tool-output compression (trailing-space strip, blank-run collapse, identical-line folding with counts) before the existing truncation cap with an honest compression note, MCP progress notifications streamed to the console as SSE frames (the single-send Telegram pipeline does not forward them, stated as such), and an editable prompt queue in the console chat — typing stays enabled while streaming, queued prompts can be edited or cancelled, and the queue dispatches in order when the turn ends. (7) Two general skills were hand-installed from an MIT-licensed upstream with per-directory SOURCE provenance and third-party product names neutralized, a new docs/security_checklist.md records the manual review posture with per-item verification commands (no comparative safety claims), and the research table now carries per-item landing marks. The site gains a web app manifest with logo icons generated from the project logo (fixing add-to-home-screen), llms.txt/robots.txt/sitemap.xml for AI readers, and a public page-view counter (Cloudflare Pages Functions + Workers KV, approximate page views stated in the payload, honest 503 when unbound — never a fake zero). Verified before these notes: the offline suite grew to 767/767 (+122 checks, previous counts unchanged) and console smoke to 110/110; an E2E script ran 35 checks to completion — all three /v1 auth states, live non-streaming and streaming completions, hooks firing real side effects on the production service pipeline (with failing hooks proven non-blocking), credential-pool rotation against a local HTTP fake upstream (401 then 200, request sequence asserted), MCP progress over a real stdio pipe, and a full ACP session over a real subprocess ending in a clean exit — with settings and secrets restored byte-for-byte. Locale packs are at 228 keys (en/zh parity), the site pack at 121, and handover/site/competitive figures were re-synced to the new counts.
